of wrath.
This gives us the picture of the community in fate, implied
by discipleship to Jesus Christ. And this is our situation as a
Christian community, as it was that of the disciples in the
hour when Jesus spoke to them His parting words. So long
as He dwelt among them, they had not truly grasped the
essence of this their situation; even in this solemn hour they
still do not realize what it means to belong to Him. They will
realize it only after He has left them. "None of you asks me:
'Where are you going?" " Their minds are fixed not on the
whither, the goal of His journey, but on the here and now
which He is leaving behind. They will be without Him,
bereft and forsaken in the world.
"Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage
that I go away." Why is it to their advantage? Because they
will not become deeply aware of their inner strength and
victory over the world so long as they have not experienced
their forsakenness in the world and the world's hostility.
Their victory? Ah, no! but the victory of Christ. Yet the
victory of Christ is to become their victory in virtue of their
discipleship to Him, their union with Him. "It is to your
advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the
Counsellor will not come to you; but if I go I will send Him
to you."
The Counsellor is none other than the Spirit of Christ, the
power which He bestows on those who belong to Him. But
they can receive the Spirit only when they have tasted the
bitterness of their abandonment. That divine power will
make itself felt in the weakness of the desolate; only out of
the sadness of their desolation in the world can they learn
to know the full measure of the victory over the world which
has been vouchsafed them. "When the Spirit of truth comes,
He will guide you into all the truth." He will lead them to
understand and be assured of their victory over the world
